items.text: Étale schemes over $k$
$X$ is étale over $k$ if it is the sum of the spectra of its points, with residue fields finite separable extensions of $k$ (reduced, in fact geometrically reduced).
Equivalent: there is a separably closed extension $k'$ of $k$ with $X_{k'}$ a constant scheme; then this holds for every such $k'$.

Proof $\Rightarrow$: $X=\coprod\operatorname{Spec}k(x)$, $X_{k'}=\coprod\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(k(x)\otimes_kk'\bigr)$, a finite product of separable extensions of $k'$, each equal to $k'$ if $k'$ is separably closed. $\Leftarrow$: reduce to $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$; $A\otimes_kk'$ finite étale over $k'$ implies $A$ finite product of finite separable extensions of $k$.
Étale $=$ geometrically constant.
Galois theory, geometrically
$k'\supset\bar k\supset k$, $\bar k$ the separable closure of $k$ in $k'$, $\Pi=\operatorname{Gal}(\bar k/k)=\varprojlim\Pi_i$ (finite groups): profinite.
X\longmapsto X(k')=X(\bar k),\qquad \{\text{étale }k\text{-schemes}\}\longrightarrow\{\text{continuous }\Pi\text{-sets}\}
Continuity: for $x\in X(\bar k)$, $\gamma\mapsto\gamma x$ factors through some finite quotient $\Pi_i$.
Theorem. This functor is an equivalence of categories. Finite inverse limits (products, fibre products) and all direct limits (quotients, sums, cokernels) correspond.
An étale group scheme $G$ over $k$ = an ordinary group $G(\bar k)$ with a continuous action of $\Pi$.
Analogy: the fundamental group and covering spaces; $\operatorname{Spec}k$ plays the role of the base space.
Hidden points

$k'/k$ finite separable of degree $n$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}k'$: one point, but $X(\bar k)$ has $n$ points; $X_{\bar k}$ has $n$ points: $X$ is arithmetically connected but not geometrically connected (an $n$-sheeted covering of $\operatorname{Spec}k$).
$k'/k$ purely inseparable: still one point after extension, with nilpotents; the multiplicity is $[k':k]=$ the length.
Morphisms into étale schemes
$T$ étale over $k$, $X$ any $k$-scheme. If $T=I_k$ is constant (trivial $\Pi$-action on $I$):
X=\coprod_{i\in I}X_i\ \ (\text{open and closed})\ \Longleftrightarrow\ X\to T=\coprod_I\operatorname{Spec}k;\qquad X\ \text{connected}\Rightarrow\text{constant, one index }i
T_{\bar k}=I_{\bar k},\quad I=T(\bar k);\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_k(X,T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Pi}\bigl(X_{\bar k},T_{\bar k}\bigr)
The scheme of geometric connected components
$X_{\bar k}$ locally connected: $X_{\bar k}=\coprod_{i\in\pi_0(X_{\bar k})}X_i$; $I=\pi_0(X_{\bar k})$ is a $\Pi$-set (continuous if $X$ is coherent, i.e. quasi-compact and quasi-separated).
$T=\pi_0(X/k)$ := the étale scheme with $T(\bar k)=\pi_0(X_{\bar k})$ (scheme of geometric connected components).
X\xrightarrow{\ \ }T=\pi_0(X/k):\ \text{surjective, with geometrically connected fibres;}\ \ T\ \text{finite étale if }X\text{ of finite type}
Characterisation 1: factorisation of $X\to T$ as a surjection with geometrically connected fibres followed by an étale morphism is unique.
Characterisation 2 (universal property): every morphism from $X$ to an étale $k$-scheme $T'$ factors uniquely through $T$.
Characterisation 3 (functor of points): for $S'$ over $k$,
T(S')=\{\,C\subset X_{S'}\ \text{open and closed}:\ C\to S'\ \text{has non-empty geometrically connected fibres}\,\}
